title: France vs Mexico: 43 dishes you should try | CNN
text:
Sign up forUnlocking the World, CNN Travel’s weekly newsletter. Get news about destinations, plus the latest in aviation, food and drink, and where to stay.

Source: CNN

In our roundup of travel stories this week: why mosquitoes are getting better at outsmarting humans, the sun-kissed island known as the “Turkish Maldives,” plus the mysterious case of the missing Korean trash cans.

Tacos or tarte tatin? Burritos or boeuf Bourguignon? Choose your fighter as we’re going all in on a battle of national fare.

France has the haute cuisine, the Michelin pedigree and the UNESCO-recognized bread.

Mexico has the confluence of Indigenous and European influences, the slow-cooked meat, and the pre-Hispanic corn processes.

We’ve put together a roundup of 20classic French disheseveryone needs to try and, because we were feeling generous, 23Mexican dishesthat ought to be on your table ASAP.

Following up with the cheese course, we havecancoillotte, a 2,000-year-old low-fat, high-protein cheese currently taking over French dairy aisles.

For US-based subscribers, we also have a two-tier dessert: The full CNN Original series ofEva Longoria: Searching for MexicoandEva Longoria: Searching for Franceare available to stream right now.

Stay safe out there this summer. Video captured recently in Botswana shows the terrifying moment a tourist boat had to outpace a charging hippo.Take a look: Its butterfly stroke is Olympic level.

On the smaller end of the scale, scientists are discovering mosquitoes are smarter than we thought. The blood-besotted blighters are theworld’s deadliest animal, and they’ve developed plenty of tricks to tap our veins, including remembering people who’ve tried to swat them.

And now we go tinier again, with a warning about microscopic pathogens. Louisiana health officials are urging Gulf Coast beachgoers to take precautions amid a surge in infections caused by aflesh-eating bacteriafound in coastal waters. Vibrio vulnificus thrive in heat and this past July was thehottest monthin the US since records began.

Continuing our countdown ofAmerica’s Best Towns to Visit in 2026, we haveBethlehem, Pennsylvania, at No. 4.

August is here, the days are getting shorter — shouldn’t you be thinking of getting the Christmas tree down from the attic? Or better yet, take a trip to Bethlehem, a former American steel town with serious holiday spirit.

“The festivities begin early here,” the manager of one of two Christmas-themed stores open year-round on Main Street tells CNN. “It’s like living in a snow globe or a Hallmark movie.”

Bethlehem’s rich legacy as a historic 18th-centuryMoravian settlementhas also earned recognition asone of the United States’ newest UNESCO World Heritage sites.

Take a look, too, at the rest of our list so far:Roanoke, Virginia, at No. 10,Lawrence, Kansas, at No. 9,Iowa City, Iowaat No. 8,Juneau, Alaska, at No. 7,Burlington, Vermont, at No. 6 andFort Collins, Colorado, at No. 5.

It’s never too early to start planning your 2027 vacation.

Less than an hour off the coast of the Turkish Riviera liesSuluada–- a remote island so strikingly white and blue it’s earned the nickname “the Turkish Maldives.” Accessible only by boat and completely untouched, CNN’s Leroy Ah Ben explores this gem known mostly to locals.

Uganda’sSsese Islandsare one of the few places in the world where a tropical archipelago sits inside a landlocked country. In the middle of Lake Victoria, Africa’s largest lake, the islands are a magical landscape where locals and pilgrims connect with ancient spirits at a sacred waterfall.

Seoul is a city of nearly 10 million people, but there are just 7,000public trash canson its streets. CNN’s Yoonjung Seo went on a mission to find the nearest receptacle.

Tourists visiting Japan also struggle to find trash cans but thereasonsbehind that are very different.
